producer.method: Hand-written by the Dokimos evaluator from the original requirement excerpts only (tests/fixtures/construction/time-entry-timer/sources/). The decide and sequence cases restate DOK-ORACLE-TIMER-1 with the same IDs, citations and requirement keys. No candidate implementation, generated code, construction plan or manifest was consulted.

subject.notes: Arm-neutral: both the baseline (an agent's own F# implementation) and the treatment (Ordo-generated code plus bounded handwritten code) are driven through the same minimal adapter. The empty state is named NoTimer (the source diagram calls it Idle).

decide.signature: state: string -> command: string -> Result<string * string list, string>
decide.meaning: Ok (nextState, effects) when the command is accepted, Error reason when it is refused.

recordedMinutes.meaning: Closed segments (start, end) in whole seconds from an arbitrary epoch. None = nothing is recorded; Some n = n whole minutes recorded.

derivedFrom.remainder: Only the single-instance reading is checked; whether one timer is allowed per person or per session is not decided by the source text.

Observed: an accepted stop, and nothing else, requests entry completion (decide); elapsed seconds from segments rounded to the nearest whole minute, exact by the minute with no six-minute unit at recording time (recordedMinutes). Not observed: the shared Commands.create path, TimerSegments provenance, and whether the candidate's own stop path calls the same arithmetic it exposes through the adapter. The excerpt states no rule for an exact half-minute tie, so no case has a total of whole minutes plus exactly 30 seconds.

Observed: repeated pause/resume cycles are legal (decide) and recordedMinutes sums only the closed working segments it is given, excluding the gaps between them. Not observed: how the candidate opens and closes segments against a clock.
The adapter contract exposes no port or persistence surface, so per-session placement is not observable through it. TIMER-ORACLE-015 (port surface) is therefore not restated; see excludedCases.

The excerpt says nothing is recorded, but the approved ECIR blueprint records CONFLICT-TIMER-SHORT-STOP (refusal versus return to NoTimer). Its cases are unscored: the candidate's answer is reported as agent-decided behavior on an unresolved conflict and never counted as pass or fail.

excludedCases.reason: A port-surface case of the Ordo naming binding. The adapter contract deliberately exposes no ports, so it is not observable through this oracle and is not restated.
